featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Bhandup Central Restaurant, and while the ambiance was just okay, the standout feature was undoubtedly the non-vegetarian tandoori items.

The decor and atmosphere were quite average, lacking any distinctive flair or charm. The seating was comfortable enough, but the overall environment felt a bit underwhelming. However, what the restaurant lacked in ambiance, it more than made up for with its delicious tandoori offerings.

The tandoori chicken was succulent and perfectly marinated, with just the right amount of spice. Each bite was a delightful explosion of flavors, cooked to perfection in the traditional tandoor oven. The lamb kebabs were equally impressive, tender and juicy with a smoky finish that left a lasting impression. The variety of tandoori dishes available catered to different palates, ensuring there was something for everyone to enjoy.

The service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was pleasant despite the unremarkable surroundings.

In conclusion, Bhandup Central Restaurant may not win any awards for its ambiance, but it is definitely worth a visit for its excellent non-vegetarian tandoori items. If you're a fan of well-cooked, flavorful tandoori dishes, this place won't disappoint.

Overall, it is good place for lunch/dinner.

Dessert options are equally impressive, featuring unique treats like kiwi halwa and traditional favorites such as gulab jamun and shrikhand. The attentive and courteous staff contribute significantly to the overall positive dining experience, ensuring guests feel welcomed and well-cared-for.

Overall, Madhuban Pure Veg Buffet provides a delightful and satisfying dining experience, making it a highly recommended destination for those seeking quality vegetarian cuisine in Mumbai.

Visited The Food Studio near Nahur Railway Station and had a generally pleasant experience. We were seated within 5 minutes, and the ambiance was nice with a large TV setup in the center, adding a lively vibe to the place.

We started with French fries and a few starters: Jhinga Koliwada, Makhmali Kumbh, Pomfret Tandoori, and Chicken Burnt Garlic. The Jhinga Koliwada was the highlight—crispy and flavorful. Makhmali Kumbh is a great vegetarian option, stuffed with cheese and tasted quite good. However, the Pomfret Tandoori didn’t meet expectations—the masala lacked punch.

For the main course, we ordered Sabzi Peshawari with roti. It leaned towards the sweeter side, possibly due to the mix of paneer, mushrooms, and green peas. Not bad if you enjoy mildly sweet gravies.

We also tried the mocktail Mulokai under their Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer. The taste was average.

Overall, a good experience with room for a few improvements.

featured_reviews.name: dhawal gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Bayroute in Cuffe Parade is less like walking into a restaurant and more like embarking on an enchanting journey across the Mediterranean and Middle East. From the moment you cross the threshold, the attention to detail in the ambience, the authentic depth of the cuisine, and the seamless service work in perfect harmony to deliver an unforgettable fine-dining experience.

The Ambience: An Arabian Night's Dream
The ambience at Bayroute is truly its soul, beautifully capturing the old-world charm and opulence of the Levant. The decor is a magnificent blend of Moroccan, Turkish, and Arabian influences. Warm, rich lighting spills over intricately patterned floor tiles and tastefully adorned walls, which feature beautiful Turkish art. The seating is plush and comfortable, with Moroccan printed sofas that invite a leisurely, communal dining experience.

The entire space exudes a refined yet cozy atmosphere—perfect for a romantic evening, a sophisticated family dinner, or celebrating a special occasion. It’s an aesthetically curated masterpiece where every corner offers a visual delight, transporting you far away from the hustle of Mumbai.

The Food: An Authentic and Flavorful Expedition
The menu is an extensive map of culinary delights from countries like Egypt, Turkey, Lebanon, and Greece. It's a testament to authentic, well-researched cuisine, and every dish we tried was a revelation.The ingredients taste fresh, and the authentic spices are used with a delicate hand, ensuring the dishes are flavorful without being overwhelmingly heavy.

The Service: Courteous and Impeccable

A superb meal is only elevated by excellent service, and Bayroute truly shines here. The staff is exceptionally courteous, knowledgeable, and attentive. Our server was well-versed in the menu, offering insightful recommendations and patiently explaining the different regional nuances of the dishes. The pacing of the meal was perfect—neither rushed nor slow—allowing us to fully enjoy the experience. The attention to detail, from refreshing water glasses to clearing plates promptly, was seamless and professional.

Bayrute is more than just a restaurant; it’s a cultural experience. While it is on the higher end of the pricing scale, the unparalleled ambience, the authentic and delicious food, and the impeccable, friendly service make it absolutely worth the indulgence. It remains a must-visit destination for anyone looking to sample the finest Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisine in Mumbai in a truly magnificent setting.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Middle Eastern experience in Mumbai, BAYROUTE is a place you simply can’t miss. We visited their Cuffe Parade outlet, and honestly, it felt like stepping straight into an Arabian dining room, warm, inviting, and rich in flavours.

Let’s start with their Classic Hummus, because that’s a non-negotiable order here. Creamy, smooth, and beautifully balanced, it’s topped with pine nuts, finished with labneh, and generously drizzled with good quality extra virgin olive oil. Simple, classic, and done perfectly, exactly how hummus should be.

For a refreshing sip, we tried their Reyhan, a soft beverage made with muddled orange and basil. Super refreshing, fragrant, and a great palate cleanser alongside the heavier dishes.

The Cheese Manakeesh was another standout. A soft Middle Eastern flatbread brushed with olive oil, loaded with lots of cheese. Comforting, indulgent, and perfect for sharing.

One of the highlights of the meal was the Dijaj Tria, a roasted trio of chicken kebabs featuring harissa spiced chicken, creamy shish taouk and Saffron Joojeh, served with garlic sauce, spicy schug and a punchy acili ezme dip. Every skewer brought something different to the table, and all of them were cooked beautifully.

Seafood lovers will enjoy the Butter Garlic Prawns, juicy, well-seasoned, and finished with rich garlic butter flavours without overpowering the prawns themselves.

We wrapped up with the Yemeni Mandi, which was aromatic, flavourful, and comforting, a wholesome dish that truly completes the Middle Eastern feast.

Overall, BAYROUTE delivers a genuine Arabian dining experience, from flavours to ambience. Perfect for anyone who enjoys Lebanese, Turkish, and Middle Eastern cuisine under one roof.

featured_reviews.review_text:
During my multiple visits to this hotel, I have observed that they use Delicious Fat Spread instead of real butter in their food. While butter is a dairy product made from milk,Delicious Fat Spread is made from vegetable oils, and the two have very different properties.

Although Delicious Fat Spread is also manufactured by Amul and marketed as a versatile alternative to butter, it is not the same as real Amul Butter. When I asked the hotel staff about it, they claimed they use Amul Butter — but in reality, they use Delicious Fat Spread.

This product may not be as healthy as real butter, especially for those who prefer natural dairy products. My only intention in sharing this review is to make people aware: if you order dishes here that contain butter, you may actually be served fat spread instead.

Please choose your food carefully and stay healthy.
Eat healthy, stay healthy.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Thambbi Veg Restaurant – Mulund West

If you’re looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian cuisine in Mulund, Thambbi Veg Restaurant is a must-visit. This place serves up a delightful variety of traditional dishes that are packed with flavor and made with care.

We started with their Paper Dosa, which truly lived up to its name—crisp, golden, and impressively long. It’s perfect for dosa lovers! Another crowd favorite here is the Andhra Masala Dosa, known for its spicy, flavorful filling that sets it apart from the usual masala dosa.

The South Indian Thali was wholesome and satisfying, offering a variety of classic items that balance each other perfectly. We also tried the Ragi Idli, a healthy yet tasty option that’s soft and light. Every dish was accompanied by fresh chutneys and piping hot sambar, both of which were incredibly flavorful and clearly made fresh.

A highlight of the meal was their strong, aromatic Filter Kaapi, served the traditional way—perfect to wrap up a hearty meal. And for dessert, the Payasam was rich, comforting, and not overly sweet—just right.

What made the experience even better was the courteous and attentive staff, who ensured we were comfortable and served promptly despite the busy crowd. The ambience is simple but clean and welcoming, suitable for both quick meals and family outings.

Overall, Thambbi offers a truly satisfying South Indian dining experience that delivers on taste, authenticity, and hospitality. Highly recommended for anyone craving comforting, vegetarian South Indian food in the heart of Mulund.

Before visiting Shera 2.0, I would recommend reading this review.

**1. Limited AC Seating**
If your group has 7 or more people and you're planning to sit in the AC section, be aware that the AC room is quite small. A single table can accommodate a maximum of around 6 people comfortably. Larger groups may not be able to sit together inside. During the summer season, sitting outside for a long time can also be uncomfortable.

**2. Outdoor Seating & Mosquitoes**
Since the AC seating is limited, many guests may have to sit outside. During our visit, there were quite a lot of mosquitoes, which made the experience even more uncomfortable. If you're visiting in the evening, especially during warmer months, this is something to keep in mind.

**3. Food Taste**
We visited this place after watching several reels and expected something unique. However, the food tasted pretty average and was no different from what you can find at many other restaurants. In fact, you can get similar food quality and taste at several places for a much lower price.

**4. Slow Service**
Make sure to place your order as early as possible because the waiting time is extremely long. Every order we placed took around 40–45 minutes to reach our table.

**5. Overpriced Menu**
If you're visiting thinking this is a budget-friendly dhaba, you may be disappointed. The pricing is surprisingly high. For example:

* Mojito: ₹499
* Fresh Lime Soda: ₹399

Considering the overall experience, the prices felt excessive.

**6. Staff Attitude**
Our bill was around ₹20,000 for a group of 10 people. We politely asked if any discount was available, but the staff's response felt quite rude and dismissive. It seemed as if asking a simple question was somehow inappropriate.

**Overall Experience**
From the moment we arrived, the overall vibe of the place didn't feel welcoming. Unfortunately, we had to stay due to the circumstances. Between the limited seating, mosquitoes, slow service, average food, high prices, and disappointing customer service, the overall experience did not justify the hype.

**Rating: 1/5**

World of Palates, just a few seconds from Marine Drive, is truly a hidden gem for vegetarians. Celebrating their 1st anniversary on 11th December, they’re offering a special grand menu along with exciting discounts throughout the week — the perfect time to visit. The ambience is warm, cosy and thoughtfully designed, with comfortable seating for both small gatherings and larger groups. The charming book-filled corners add a unique, aesthetic touch.

We visited during their Sunday brunch, and the spread was delightful — fresh loaf breads, hummus, tacos, vibrant salads and juicy fruits that instantly caught the eye. The mains were equally impressive, featuring creamy mac and cheese, sautéed veggies, paneer lababdar, dal tadka, biryani and noodles. The highlight was definitely the desserts, with their pancakes and waffles stealing the show. A must-visit for anyone who loves global flavours and comforting vegetarian food.

featured_reviews.name: Anita Pemgirikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Really Nice Lunch Experience

Good food, calm ambience, and a satisfying afternoon meal.

I tried their lunch buffet recently and had a genuinely good time. The dishes were fresh, flavourful, and comforting, the kind of food you actually enjoy without feeling too heavy. The live waffle and pancake counter was a lovely addition, and everything was made perfectly.

The ambience was another highlight. The place is peaceful, clean, and feels welcoming. They also have a nice variety of books you can pick up and read, which makes the whole experience even more relaxing if you like slow, cosy lunches. The service was polite and everything felt smooth and comfortable.

If you’re around Nariman Point and want a lunch that feels calming and genuinely enjoyable, this spot is definitely worth visiting. 🍽️✨

featured_reviews.name: Bhavik Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Decent food, some delicious dishes like the cheese filled broccoli and also the burrata witch sauces and bread. But this place was infamous for having slowest service possible and we experienced it that day.

featured_reviews.name: VAISHNAVI JAIN
featured_reviews.review_text: Didnot think of writing this review but i would want to really call out the behaviour of a particular waiter ‘MANISH’. Extremely rude guy and has zero etiquettes. We waited for over 40mins for the food. We ordered chilly cheese toast, the papad. 40 mins seriously? And when we complaint he literally threw the manchurian in our poates as if we were having our food for FREE. Horrible experience and worst service. I would give a ZERO FOR THE SERVICE

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
After a long and hectic day at work, our group decided to unwind and walked across from our Head Office to Worlds of Palate, a charming pure-vegetarian restaurant located right in the heart of Nariman Point. The place immediately gives a sense of calm — a cosy, tastefully done interior with soothing music and warm lighting that makes it perfect for relaxed conversations.

We ordered a spread that truly showcased the kitchen’s range: Veg Biryani, Pesto and Pesto Pizza, and Spaghetti Aglio Olio Pasta. Every dish arrived freshly prepared, beautifully plated, and perfectly balanced in flavour. The biryani was aromatic and not oily, the pizza had a crisp thin crust with a generous layer of pesto and cheese, and the pasta was cooked al dente with authentic Italian seasoning. It’s evident that the restaurant uses quality ingredients and pays attention to detail.

Service was prompt and courteous, with the staff checking in just at the right times — not intrusive, yet attentive. The portion sizes were satisfying, and prices felt reasonable for the location and ambience.

What stood out most was the peaceful atmosphere, quite unlike the busy office district around it. Worlds of Palate manages to create a small oasis of calm in the middle of Mumbai’s corporate hub — ideal for colleagues looking for a quiet dinner or even a quick team lunch.

Overall, it’s a must-visit vegetarian restaurant in Nariman Point for anyone who appreciates freshness, flavour, and a relaxed dining experience. We left refreshed, content, and sure that we'll return soon.

featured_reviews.name: Ilma Khan
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited World of Palates, Nariman Point and loved the experience! The menu offers a wide variety of global vegetarian dishes from Indian to Continental and Asian all packed with flavour. The cozy reading corners with shelves of books make it a perfect spot to relax and enjoy good food with a peaceful vibe.

featured_reviews.name: Priyansh Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Spesso Gourmet Kitchen is an absolute winner for vegetarian food, offering an extensive menu where almost everything hits the mark. Their sizzlers, soups, mixed veg and paneer platters, appetizers, Mexican dishes, and even dim sums are all top-notch — genuinely a 10/10 experience. The place is usually crowded, which says a lot about its popularity, but the food more than makes up for it. If you’re looking for a pure veg spot with consistently amazing taste, this one is highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m genuinely disappointed with my recent visit to Espresso Gourmet. It used to be a good place earlier, but the quality and overall experience have clearly declined.

The café was extremely overcrowded, which made the experience uncomfortable and affected the service.

I tried the ₹400 tiramisu and it was very disappointing — mostly cream with barely any sponge or coffee flavour. It lacked the richness and balance you expect from a proper tiramisu.

The pizza was also below average and not worth the price.

Overall, not the experience I expected based on my previous visits. I hope they improve.

featured_reviews.name: pranali Bedarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a wonderful dining experience at Spesso Gourmet Kitchen. The ambience is elegant, modern, and very welcoming, making it a perfect place for both casual meals and special occasions. The staff is courteous, attentive, and ensures you feel comfortable throughout your visit.

The food is truly impressive – beautifully presented and full of flavor. Each dish feels carefully prepared with quality ingredients and great attention to detail. The menu offers a nice variety, and everything we tried was delicious and well-balanced in taste.

Service was quick without feeling rushed, and the overall experience felt smooth and enjoyable. Spesso Gourmet Kitchen definitely stands out for its combination of great taste, presentation, and hospitality. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a premium dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Shweta Killedar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was missing Thai food and found this place on Google. Honestly, everything here feels mid — food, service, ambience — definitely not worth the price. The flavors lacked authenticity and didn’t really satisfy the Thai food craving.

The papaya salad was good, tiger prawns were decent, and the cocktails were probably the best part of the meal.

Must try: Coconut pudding

Wouldn’t recommend ordering the charcoal chicken. The steamed John Dory had a distinct smell, though the taste itself was okish.

Overall, not a place I’d recommend if you’re looking for authentic Thai food.

featured_reviews.name: RD's Find
featured_reviews.review_text: Still the gold standard for Thai food in Mumbai. We had the John Dory in garlic sauce and the Thai Green Curry, and both were spectacular—perfectly balanced flavors that stay true to authentic Thai roots. The Tub Tim Grob (water chestnut dessert) was the perfect refreshing end to the meal. It’s expensive, but for the quality and the heritage, it’s worth every rupee.

featured_reviews.name: Buck Whas
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the most authentic Thai I’ve had in India. When I saw the menu and the dishes offered of which you don’t find in typical Thai restaurants I knew I had to check it out. The yum tua poo (wing bean salad) is a gem often overlooked but is amazing and if pescatarian do try it with prawn. I spoke with the head chef who has worked to maintain Thai flavors while respecting vegetarian majority. Nonetheless you request Thai style and she will turn it out authentic Thai style. I think this might be key if dining here and you have experience with Thai cuisine is that you need to specify that you wanted to be prepared a Thai style.

featured_reviews.name: Purvi Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything from starters, mains and desserts was delicious. The team took extra care to make sure the food was non-spicy, as requested. Hard to pick one, but the desserts were delicious and very indulgent. It was my fist time tasting tub tim grob (water chestnuts in coconut milk with ice) and I loved it! We also ordered coconut pudding with sago and coconut ice cream and it was delicious too!

If you love thai food, I would highly recommend this place to you!

featured_reviews.name: Yogita N Goyal
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was authentic and very tasty. The bao Thai dish, similar to a dumpling, was soft and delicious. The Thai dessert Tub Tim Grob was too good and a perfect end to the meal. The staff was very courteous and had a great eye for detail. Service was smooth, and everything was done perfectly to make the atmosphere memorable for guests. Overall, a wonderful dining experience. It was much better experience than Taj Mahal Mumbai. Thanks to the staff.

featured_reviews.name: Neeraj Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Great food and ambience! Right intent to serve but with questionable execution. We went on 13th April evening to celebrate a birthday and after the restaurant confirmed twice with us about the special occasion,  they neither offered any celebration nor even a greeting for the birthday! After we left, I called the hotel twice to give feedback and was told that the restaurant manager will call back but that did not happen either.That is not Taj hospitality standards that we are used to and hope it was just an aberration!

featured_reviews.name: Rishi Mistry
featured_reviews.review_text: After two weeks in India, we were ready for a little break from all of the wonderful Indian food we’ve had. Staying at the President Mumbai, we decided Thai Pavilion would be a convenient change of pace. I’m so glad we gave it a shot! All of our food was delicious - some of the tastiest Thai food I’ve had outside of Thailand. We shared the lotus and banana leaf salad, the red curry with shrimp, and the spicy basil rice. Everything was so delicious and satisfying. Our server was polite and attentive. The atmosphere is nice as well. Would love to return on our next trip to Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Sachi Gandhhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Thai pavilion for dinner recently and had a great experience! Loved the great service and delicious food.

They served pumpkin chips before the meal which were so light and crispy. I really enjoyed them.

For appetisers we had the pomelo salad which was my absolute favourite dish and I definitely recommend it. We also had the corn cakes which were good but could have had little more flavour. I ordered the Tom yum soup which was spicy and nice. We also got the lotus root chips which also tasted good with the house sauces that they provide.

For mains we had the pad Thai which I felt was a little bland and could have been more flavourful along with the water chestnut in a spicy sauce.

Although we liked some dishes more than others, they service was great and I will definitely be back for my favourites!

featured_reviews.name: Indradeep Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Entry from Gate 2. Late evening normally there is not much rush and you can park on your own. Else valet is intermittently available.

Earlier there was an open air section that is now covered permanently. However, as the ceiling covers are too high you can continue to feel it as an open air space.

Visited with my friend and we wanted to have a quick drink with an appetiser and share a large plate. We opted for Kashmiri Kena which was undoubtedly wonderful with liberal sprinkle of Kashmiri spices.  In the main course we opted for their signature pot rice with chicken with sauteed vegetables. It was a bit bland although we enjoyed it for its overall portion of vegetables and the taste. You can obviously request to make it spicy in case you want to.

The host was very warm and welcome. We got a lot of help to place our orders and patiently explained about the foods that we opted for.

Importantly no noise so we had a wonderful conversation going. We loved this

Definitely a great place I would like to visit a few times with my friends and family.

There is an indoor section which can be booked for a private party. The toilet is outside the restaurant but was well maintained.

featured_reviews.name: Ariez Tata
featured_reviews.review_text: The food here is best and most flavourful cuisine I had ever eaten in a very long time! Even in a place like Mumbai which has thousands of amazing restaurants, this stood out! It was outstanding because the flavour of all the dishes was absolutely amazing! I can’t wait to go there and eat again! Check out the pictures of all the food! The Galouti kebab, sitafal ice cream and the mushroom truffle risotto were outstanding!

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Varma
featured_reviews.review_text: The restaurant is located on the ground floor of World trade centre compleax near gate no 2. They have a buffet during the lunch time which cost Rs 1200+taxes. The buffet spread is varied and has burmese, chinese, indian, continental and Nepali cuisine. They also have a live counter for chaat, paani Puri and sev puri. They also serve mocktails at the table. One of the highlights are the hand churned icecream. Overall a very good experience.

featured_reviews.name: Gautam Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice large restaurant located in the World Trade Centre Arcade on the ground floor. Have wide variety of Asian and North Indian food. The Emmental Chilli Naan as well as the Exoric Vegetables in Red Hot Garlic Sauce in Sizzling Stone Bowl were excellent. Service was superb - we reached the restaurant at 10.05 pm. featured_reviews.name: Bhavesh Kanakia

Food was quite good . Sushi was too good. Should surely try Mini falafel and khowsuey.

Overall a good experience.  Would recommend going with family and friends.

featured_reviews.name: Vini Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a fantastic experience at Fountain Sizzlers in Palladium Mall, thanks to Tahil. He provided excellent service from start to finish and really elevated our meal with his thoughtful recommendations. Every suggestion he made was spot on, and he was attentive without being overbearing.

It’s rare to come across service that genuinely enhances the dining experience, and Tahil did exactly that. We truly appreciated his professionalism, warmth, and knowledge of the menu. Looking forward to coming back again!

featured_reviews.name: Ekta Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Loved the buffet lunch! Apparently they do only buffet during lunch hours. Went for my parent’s anniversary celebration. We all enjoyed the spread. All the dishes were tasty - from cheese nachos salsa to khowsuey to Hakka noodles. Definitely visiting again. The price was also reasonable 1000pp

featured_reviews.name: vibhor borkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flamboyante – A stunning blend of style, flavor, and ambience 🍸🌿
Flamboyante, located at World Trade Centre, Cuffe Parade, is one of Mumbai’s most elegant dining destinations. The restaurant offers a beautiful mix of Mediterranean, Asian, and Indian cuisines, all served in a setting that’s as sophisticated as it is relaxed. The décor is lush and artistic.

Every dish is crafted with attention to detail — from wood-fired pizzas and sushi to grilled kebabs, chats, paani puries and mocktails, everything tastes fresh and flavorful. The service is professional yet friendly, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable.

Tips:

Book a table in advance, especially for dinner or weekends.

Perfect for romantic celebrations, or elegant brunches.

Request: Please add biriyani in then non veg section.

A classy spot that truly lives up to its name — flamboyant and unforgettable! ✨🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Yash Popat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Trattoria at Taj President, Cuffe Parade, Mumbai, is one of the city’s most iconic Italian restaurants that has recently undergone a renovation. The place looks lovely with warm interiors, elegant lighting, and an atmosphere that feels both modern and classic.

As for the food, it was a mixed experience. The Spinach & Ricotta Cannelloni was genuinely enjoyable, creamy and well-balanced. However, the asparagus pizza was a letdown. It felt more Indianised than authentic Italian, and lacked flavor. To make matters worse, despite ordering just two mains, the waiter mixed up the order, bringing a thin crust pizza instead of the medium crust we had asked for, and also forgot the house bread basket.

Overall, while Trattoria still carries its old-world charm and reputation, the food and service didn’t quite match the expectations of a Taj classic. Hopefully, they can bring back the authenticity and attention to detail that made it a favorite for so many over the years.
